summary: Boolean applies JavaScript truthiness rules and returns a primitive Boolean.
documentation: Boolean applies JavaScript truthiness rules and returns a primitive Boolean. Zero, empty strings, null and false are falsey among JSON values. Arrays and objects are truthy even when empty, unlike Python’s empty-container rules.
returns: One truth-value Boolean for each input item.
caution: Boolean("false") is true because the string is nonempty. This does not parse textual configuration labels, and new Boolean creates an object rather than the primitive used here.
scenarios: Convert a local expression result into an explicit flag.
Explain why empty collections still pass a JavaScript truth check.
Audit form-preview logic that mixes string labels and Boolean values.
title: Apply JavaScript truth-value rules
problem: Return Boolean(item) for every input value in order. Empty arrays and objects must be true; the string false is also true. Do not interpret text labels.
hint: Call Boolean as a function, without new.
goal: Use Boolean() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
